title: Bars and Pubs
goal: Order a drink, ask about the choices and payment, buy a round, or decline another drink.

study.title: More drinks or the end of service

runs.text: asks whether someone wants the same drink again. Reply
announces a final opportunity to order before service ends. It is not a request that you must buy another drink.

runs.text: I said no. I don't want another drink
makes the boundary explicit. An explanation is optional.
Speak both roles when practicing alone. Use the menu above; for tab practice, the fictional bartender allows tabs and asks for the customer's name.
Order a glass of white wine and a sparkling water. Ask whether to pay now; staff answer
Order a gin and tonic without ice. Staff ask about lime; choose yes or no.
Change the response: the lager is unavailable. Staff offer bottled beer or sparkling water. Choose one, or decline the order.
Offer a round to two friends. One wants cola; the other does not want a drink. Place the resulting order, including your own mocktail.
Start a tab under the name Dana. Later, last call is announced. Decline another drink and ask to close the tab.
Hide the models. Ask about one choice, order, and respond when a companion offers another drink. Repeat with the opposite choice about having another.
A glass of the house white wine and a sparkling water, please. Should I pay now?
Could I get a gin and tonic with no ice? — Lime? — Yes, please.
This round's on me. What would you like?
One cola and one lime-and-mint mocktail, please.
Can I start a tab? The name is Dana.
No more drinks, thanks. I'd like to close out my tab.
Did the serving and drink match the order? Did a declined drink stay declined? Did you distinguish ordering another drink from paying for the drinks already ordered?
